pathway.title: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage has eased, but only through earnings. Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. carries debt principal of USD 5,148.8 million at June 30, 2026 against USD 5,148.9 million at December 31, 2025, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 544.3 million against USD 504.8 million for FY2025. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is therefore 9.46x, down from 10.20x, and 9.11x net of USD 192.1 million of cash. Because principal has not moved, leverage will rise as quickly as it fell if earnings decline: a 10% fall in trailing Adjusted EBITDA would put the ratio at about 10.51x (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the sensitivity). The measure is the issuer's own non-GAAP figure, stated after site lease expense, and the covenant definition is not supplied.

Cash interest cover is above 1.0x but not by much. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid of USD 390.1 million 1.40x on the trailing basis, against 1.28x for FY2025 and 1.09x for FY2024, and covered net interest expense 1.37x. After capital expenditure of USD 76.1 million, Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest about 1.20x, and trailing free cash flow is USD 84.3 million. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA could fall by about 28.3% before cash interest cover reaches 1.0x, and the issuer's own estimate of cash interest of about USD 394 million in 2027 would give cover of about 1.38x on trailing earnings (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). Cash flow and cash interest include discontinued operations, so the cover is indicative.

Secured debt is most of the stack. First-priority secured debt is USD 3,340.0 million, or 6.14x trailing Adjusted EBITDA and about 64.9% of principal, made up of a USD 425.0 million term loan and USD 2,915.0 million of senior secured notes due 2030, 2031 and 2033. The USD 1,805.3 million of senior unsecured notes due in 2028 and 2029 are effectively subordinated to that debt and structurally subordinated to non-guarantors, and the guarantor list is not supplied. The ratio is an indicator of secured leverage, not the covenant measure.

Liquidity is adequate for now, with the main maturities two years away. Cash is USD 192.1 million and excess availability under the revolver and receivables-based facility is USD 205.5 million, together USD 397.6 million, with no borrowings drawn and both facilities maturing June 12, 2030. That sum is about one year of the issuer's expected 2027 cash interest. Availability under the receivables-based facility depends on a borrowing base, and the revolver's springing first lien net leverage covenant of 7.10x was not in effect at June 30, 2026, so headroom cannot be measured. The next significant maturities are USD 1,324.6 million in 2028 (the 7.750% notes and the term loan) and USD 906.3 million in 2029, which together are about 43.3% of principal.

The pending merger dominates the capital structure outlook. The take-private merger at USD 2.43 per share was approved by stockholders on May 12, 2026 and was expected to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026, but its first outside date of November 9, 2026 falls four days after the cutoff and the supplied sources do not say whether it closed. Debt amendments make the merger not a change of control, but they become operative only on closing, and conditional redemption notices cover the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes. The funding source and price of those redemptions and the buyer's financing are not supplied. Equity consideration on basic shares is about USD 1,237.1 million, about 24.0% of debt principal, so the offer implies a thin equity layer beneath the debt (Analyst Interpretation; no valuation or recovery view is stated).

Business risk is short-cycle revenue against fixed rent. Roadside advertising is mostly sold in four-week periods while site leases and municipal and airport concessions run for years, so a demand dip reaches margin before contracts roll. Airports Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.3% in H1 2026 against 41.0% for America because airport site lease expense was 59.2% of revenue, and airport minimum guarantees rise with prior-period performance. Revenue grew 8.7% in the second quarter of 2026 and Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.6%, partly on event-driven demand from the FIFA World Cup (Documentary Fact; the event effect is Analyst Interpretation as to repeatability).

runs.text: Strengths. Earnings momentum: trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 544.3 million is above the FY2025 level of USD 504.8 million, and H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA grew about 19.0% over H1 2025 (Documentary Fact). Permit-protected, diversified inventory: more than 64,500 displays and operations in 81 U.S. markets at December 31, 2025, and no single advertiser is a material portion of revenue (Documentary Fact; the leading-position claims are Management Language and are not adopted). Liquidity and runway: USD 192.1 million of cash, USD 205.5 million of undrawn facilities maturing in June 2030, and no significant maturities before 2028 (Documentary Fact). Simplified, domestic business: substantially all international operations were sold, with the Spain sale completed on August 4, 2026, which simplifies the perimeter (Documentary Fact). No distributions: no dividends are intended and none are permitted while the merger agreement stands (Documentary Fact). Positive free cash flow: USD 84.3 million on the trailing basis against USD 32.0 million in FY2025 (Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the measure).

Weaknesses. High leverage with flat debt: 9.46x total debt and 9.11x net, with principal essentially unchanged, so deleveraging relies on earnings and asset sale proceeds (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). Thin cover: cash interest cover of 1.40x and about 1.20x after capital expenditure leave limited room for an advertising downturn, and the stockholders' deficit is USD 3,457.1 million (Documentary Fact). Fixed airport rent: airport site lease expense at 59.2% of revenue makes the fastest-growing segment the lowest-margin one, and USD 1,361.9 million of operating lease liabilities sit outside the debt figure (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Refinancing concentration: about 43.3% of principal falls due in 2028 and 2029, and the unsecured notes rank behind USD 3,340.0 million of secured debt (Documentary Fact). Metro and sector concentration: America is about three quarters of revenue, Los Angeles is a leading market, and 2026 growth drew on technology advertisers in the San Francisco area (Documentary Fact). Unresolved ownership and merger outcome: control, merger financing, the post-closing capital plan and the consent terms are not supplied, and willingness of the prospective owner cannot be inferred from its identity (Insufficient Information). Information limits: covenant headroom, guarantor financials and executed documents are not supplied (Insufficient Information).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The pending transaction is the take-private merger. On February 9, 2026 the company agreed to be acquired by an investor consortium of affiliates and/or certain investment funds advised by Mubadala Capital through Madison Parent Inc. and Madison Merger Sub Inc., with Merger Sub merging into the company, which would survive as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (S1 page:4; S4 page:8). Holders of common stock would receive 2.43 per share in cash. The Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired on April 9, 2026 and stockholders approved the agreement on May 12, 2026 (S4 page:8). The latest filing says closing is expected by the end of the third quarter of 2026, subject to remaining customary conditions including review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (S4 page:8). The annual report adds termination rights if the merger is not consummated on or before November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if requisite regulatory approvals are not obtained, a termination fee payable by the company of 39.8 million, or 19.9 million during the go-shop period, and a fee payable by Parent of 92.9 million under certain other circumstances (S1 page:24; S1 page:53; S1 page:54). The company has represented that the buyer has sufficient funds, but it also warns that the equity and debt financing contemplated by the merger agreement must be funded or closed (S1 page:24). The financing amounts, the sources of the buyer's equity and the post-closing capital structure are Not supplied. Until closing, the agreement restricts the company from incurring certain debt, paying dividends, settling certain proceedings and incurring certain capital expenditures without the buyer's written consent (S1 page:25). The first outside date, November 9, 2026, falls four days after the cutoff of November 5, 2026, and nothing in the supplied sources reports whether the merger closed or the dates moved.

The merger has direct debt consequences, all described as pending at August 5, 2026. In April 2026 the company completed consent solicitations with holders of its senior secured notes and with the lenders under its credit agreement, and in May 2026 with the lenders under its receivables-based credit agreement, entering into supplemental indentures and amendments dated April 9, April 10 and May 15, 2026 (S4 page:8; S4 page:9; S4 page:38; S4 page:39). These provide that the merger will not constitute a change of control under the debt documents; the supplemental indentures and the credit agreement amendment are effective but become operative only on consummation of the merger, and cease to be effective if it is not completed (S4 page:16). The receivables-based amendment, when effective, would extend the maturity of that facility to five years from the merger, raise revolving commitments from 200.0 million to 250.0 million, broaden the borrowing base and permit qualified securitisation financings (S4 page:16; S4 page:17). The company has also issued conditional notices of redemption for the 7.750% Senior Notes due 2028 and the 7.500% Senior Notes due 2029, conditional on closing (S4 page:17). Together these actions would remove the 2028 and 2029 unsecured maturities and keep the secured notes outstanding with changed change-of-control terms, but the consent terms, the redemption price and the source of redemption funds are Not supplied, and the executed supplemental indentures and amendments are cited in the exhibit list but not supplied (S4 page:38; S4 page:39). No new debt was issued in the first half of 2026: the six-month cash flow shows 145 thousand of debt repayments and no issuance line (S4 page:5).

Earlier new debt issues explain the current stack. In March 2024 the company issued 865.0 million of 7.875% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 and used part of the proceeds to prepay 835.0 million of its term loan, refinancing the remaining 425.0 million and extending its maturity to August 2028 (S1 page:69; S1 page:107). On August 4, 2025 it issued 1,150.0 million of 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and 900.0 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2033, and with cash on hand redeemed 1,250.0 million of 5.125% and 750.0 million of 9.000% senior secured notes; it paid 62.0 million of accrued interest, a 36.1 million redemption premium and 26.3 million of other fees, and recognised a 43.8 million loss on extinguishment (S1 page:69; S1 page:102). In June 2025 it extended the revolving and receivables-based facilities to June 12, 2030, reduced the revolver from 115.8 million to 100.0 million and raised the receivables-based facility from 175.0 million to 200.0 million (S1 page:102). In the second quarter of 2025 it repurchased 95.7 million of 7.750% and 134.1 million of 7.500% senior notes in the open market for 203.4 million including accrued interest and fees, recognising a gain of 28.8 million; the repurchased notes are held by the company and not cancelled (S1 page:102). The debt register, maturities and liquidity are in the CP-1 handoff: principal is 5,148.8 million at June 30, 2026 and no significant maturities fall before 2028.

The disposal programme is the other transaction thread. The company sold Switzerland, Italy and France in 2023, Mexico, Peru and Chile on February 5, 2025 for 34.0 million, the Europe-North segment to Bauer Radio Limited on March 31, 2025 for 625.0 million (net cash proceeds 572.0 million, part used to prepay the 375.0 million CCIBV term loan), and Brazil on October 1, 2025 for 15.0 million (S1 page:93; S1 page:94). It used proceeds and cash on hand to reduce indebtedness by approximately 605 million in 2025 (S1 page:55). The Spain sale agreed on September 7, 2025 for approximately 115 million euros (S2 page:9; S1 page:94) completed on August 4, 2026 for a purchase price of approximately 132.3 million dollars, with net proceeds subject to adjustments and fees; the company intends to use them to reduce debt, subject to the outcome of the merger (S4 page:9; S4 page:22). That completion is a subsequent event to the June 30, 2026 balance sheet and is not in the balance-sheet figures. At the offer price, equity consideration on 509,093,845 basic shares outstanding at July 31, 2026 is about 1,237.1 million before equity awards and any other dilutive instruments (C2); the supplied sources do not state the fully diluted equity value or the enterprise value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is a highly leveraged, now almost entirely U.S. out-of-home advertiser whose reported earnings are improving while its debt stack is unchanged. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA of 544.3 for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 (FY2025 of 504.8 plus H1 2026 of 247.3 less H1 2025 of 207.8), debt principal including finance leases of 5,148.8 is 9.46x and, net of 192.1 of continuing cash, 9.11x, down from 10.20x and 9.82x at FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid of 390.1 only 1.40x, against 1.28x for FY2025 and 1.09x for FY2024. Revenue for the twelve months is 1,679.1 against 1,604.1 for FY2025, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin is 32.4%. Free cash flow, defined here as operating cash flow of 160.4 less capital expenditures of 76.1, is 84.3; both inputs include discontinued operations. Debt principal barely changed between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026: every note and term-loan balance is identical, and only finance leases moved, down 0.1. So the leverage improvement is earnings-led. The structure is 3,340.0 of first-priority secured debt (a 425.0 term loan and 2,915.0 of senior secured notes), 1,805.3 of senior unsecured notes due 2028 and 2029, and undrawn facilities; the secured share of principal is high, and the unsecured notes are effectively subordinated to it. Liquidity is 192.1 of cash and 205.5 of excess availability under a 100.0 revolving facility and a 200.0 receivables-based facility, both maturing June 12, 2030. The next significant maturities are in 2028, when 899.3 of 7.750% senior notes and the 425.0 term loan fall due, and the company has issued conditional redemption notices for the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes, with conditions that include the merger closing. Operating lease liabilities of 1,361.9 and 877.6 of non-lease non-cancelable contracts at December 31, 2025 sit outside debt. Three qualifications bound this view. First, Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's non-GAAP measure and is stated after site lease expense; the covenant EBITDA is not supplied. Second, cash-flow figures include the Spain business that was held for sale and the 2025 cash flows of businesses sold in 2025. Third, nothing after August 5, 2026 is supplied, so the merger, the redemption notices and the use of Spain sale proceeds, which are described as pending, cannot be reflected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is a listed U.S. out-of-home advertising operator with no controlling holder identified in the supplied sources, whose creditor story is a simplified, almost entirely domestic business sitting under a heavy, mostly unchanged debt stack while a take-private merger is pending. The operating base is roadside billboards and street furniture in the America segment and airport concessions in the Airports segment, together more than 64,500 displays at June 30, 2026, with digital displays a small share of inventory but a large share of revenue. Revenue is sold in short periods, mostly four weeks in roadside, against site leases and municipal and airport concessions that run for years with minimum guaranteed payments, so revenue visibility is short while the main cost is fixed or semi-fixed. That asymmetry is sharper in Airports, where site lease expense was 59.2% of revenue in H1 2026 against 31.3% in America (C1), so airport growth carries more fixed rent. Seasonality is steady: first quarter weakest and fourth quarter strongest. The credit-relevant history is a multi-year exit from international markets, completed with the sale of Spain on August 4, 2026, and a sequence of refinancings that moved secured maturities out to 2031 and 2033 while leaving the unsecured notes in 2028 and 2029. The transaction that matters most is the merger signed on February 9, 2026 with Madison Parent Inc., at 2.43 per share in cash, approved by stockholders on May 12, 2026 and expected, per the latest filing, to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026. The merger agreement lets either party terminate if closing has not happened by November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if regulatory approvals are outstanding, so the cutoff of November 5, 2026 falls four days before the first outside date, and the supplied sources do not say whether closing occurred. Debt amendments and conditional redemption notices tied to the merger exist, but they are described as pending. Ownership of the equity after closing, the merger financing, and the executed debt documents are not supplied. Documented issuer actions so far are mostly supportive or neutral for creditors, with disposal proceeds applied to debt and no dividends; none of the creditor-adverse actions in the method's checklist is documented in the supplied filings, which is a statement about the sources, not a finding about the executed documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending transaction is the take-private merger. On February 9, 2026 the company agreed to be acquired by an investor consortium of affiliates and/or certain investment funds advised by Mubadala Capital through Madison Parent Inc. and Madison Merger Sub Inc., with Merger Sub merging into the company, which would survive as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (S1 page:4; S4 page:8). Holders of common stock would receive 2.43 per share in cash. The Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired on April 9, 2026 and stockholders approved the agreement on May 12, 2026 (S4 page:8). The latest filing says closing is expected by the end of the third quarter of 2026, subject to remaining customary conditions including review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (S4 page:8). The annual report adds termination rights if the merger is not consummated on or before November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if requisite regulatory approvals are not obtained, a termination fee payable by the company of 39.8 million, or 19.9 million during the go-shop period, and a fee payable by Parent of 92.9 million under certain other circumstances (S1 page:24; S1 page:53; S1 page:54). The company has represented that the buyer has sufficient funds, but it also warns that the equity and debt financing contemplated by the merger agreement must be funded or closed (S1 page:24). The financing amounts, the sources of the buyer's equity and the post-closing capital structure are Not supplied. Until closing, the agreement restricts the company from incurring certain debt, paying dividends, settling certain proceedings and incurring certain capital expenditures without the buyer's written consent (S1 page:25). The first outside date, November 9, 2026, falls four days after the cutoff of November 5, 2026, and nothing in the supplied sources reports whether the merger closed or the dates moved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The merger has direct debt consequences, all described as pending at August 5, 2026. In April 2026 the company completed consent solicitations with holders of its senior secured notes and with the lenders under its credit agreement, and in May 2026 with the lenders under its receivables-based credit agreement, entering into supplemental indentures and amendments dated April 9, April 10 and May 15, 2026 (S4 page:8; S4 page:9; S4 page:38; S4 page:39). These provide that the merger will not constitute a change of control under the debt documents; the supplemental indentures and the credit agreement amendment are effective but become operative only on consummation of the merger, and cease to be effective if it is not completed (S4 page:16). The receivables-based amendment, when effective, would extend the maturity of that facility to five years from the merger, raise revolving commitments from 200.0 million to 250.0 million, broaden the borrowing base and permit qualified securitisation financings (S4 page:16; S4 page:17). The company has also issued conditional notices of redemption for the 7.750% Senior Notes due 2028 and the 7.500% Senior Notes due 2029, conditional on closing (S4 page:17). Together these actions would remove the 2028 and 2029 unsecured maturities and keep the secured notes outstanding with changed change-of-control terms, but the consent terms, the redemption price and the source of redemption funds are Not supplied, and the executed supplemental indentures and amendments are cited in the exhibit list but not supplied (S4 page:38; S4 page:39). No new debt was issued in the first half of 2026: the six-month cash flow shows 145 thousand of debt repayments and no issuance line (S4 page:5).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier new debt issues explain the current stack. In March 2024 the company issued 865.0 million of 7.875% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 and used part of the proceeds to prepay 835.0 million of its term loan, refinancing the remaining 425.0 million and extending its maturity to August 2028 (S1 page:69; S1 page:107). On August 4, 2025 it issued 1,150.0 million of 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and 900.0 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2033, and with cash on hand redeemed 1,250.0 million of 5.125% and 750.0 million of 9.000% senior secured notes; it paid 62.0 million of accrued interest, a 36.1 million redemption premium and 26.3 million of other fees, and recognised a 43.8 million loss on extinguishment (S1 page:69; S1 page:102). In June 2025 it extended the revolving and receivables-based facilities to June 12, 2030, reduced the revolver from 115.8 million to 100.0 million and raised the receivables-based facility from 175.0 million to 200.0 million (S1 page:102). In the second quarter of 2025 it repurchased 95.7 million of 7.750% and 134.1 million of 7.500% senior notes in the open market for 203.4 million including accrued interest and fees, recognising a gain of 28.8 million; the repurchased notes are held by the company and not cancelled (S1 page:102). The debt register, maturities and liquidity are in the CP-1 handoff: principal is 5,148.8 million at June 30, 2026 and no significant maturities fall before 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The disposal programme is the other transaction thread. The company sold Switzerland, Italy and France in 2023, Mexico, Peru and Chile on February 5, 2025 for 34.0 million, the Europe-North segment to Bauer Radio Limited on March 31, 2025 for 625.0 million (net cash proceeds 572.0 million, part used to prepay the 375.0 million CCIBV term loan), and Brazil on October 1, 2025 for 15.0 million (S1 page:93; S1 page:94). It used proceeds and cash on hand to reduce indebtedness by approximately 605 million in 2025 (S1 page:55). The Spain sale agreed on September 7, 2025 for approximately 115 million euros (S2 page:9; S1 page:94) completed on August 4, 2026 for a purchase price of approximately 132.3 million dollars, with net proceeds subject to adjustments and fees; the company intends to use them to reduce debt, subject to the outcome of the merger (S4 page:9; S4 page:22). That completion is a subsequent event to the June 30, 2026 balance sheet and is not in the balance-sheet figures. At the offer price, equity consideration on 509,093,845 basic shares outstanding at July 31, 2026 is about 1,237.1 million before equity awards and any other dilutive instruments (C2); the supplied sources do not state the fully diluted equity value or the enterprise value.

fields.value: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is a highly leveraged advertising credit whose earnings are improving while its debt is unchanged, and a pending take-private merger leaves its capital structure unresolved. fields.value: Cash interest cover is above 1.0x but not by much. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid of USD 390.1 million 1.40x on the trailing basis, against 1.28x for FY2025 and 1.09x for FY2024, and covered net interest expense 1.37x. After capital expenditure of USD 76.1 million, Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest about 1.20x, and trailing free cash flow is USD 84.3 million. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA could fall by about 28.3% before cash interest cover reaches 1.0x, and the issuer's own estimate of cash interest of about USD 394 million in 2027 would give cover of about 1.38x on trailing earnings (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). Cash flow and cash interest include discontinued operations, so the cover is indicative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Secured debt is most of the stack. First-priority secured debt is USD 3,340.0 million, or 6.14x trailing Adjusted EBITDA and about 64.9% of principal, made up of a USD 425.0 million term loan and USD 2,915.0 million of senior secured notes due 2030, 2031 and 2033. The USD 1,805.3 million of senior unsecured notes due in 2028 and 2029 are effectively subordinated to that debt and structurally subordinated to non-guarantors, and the guarantor list is not supplied. The ratio is an indicator of secured leverage, not the covenant measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for now, with the main maturities two years away. Cash is USD 192.1 million and excess availability under the revolver and receivables-based facility is USD 205.5 million, together USD 397.6 million, with no borrowings drawn and both facilities maturing June 12, 2030. That sum is about one year of the issuer's expected 2027 cash interest. Availability under the receivables-based facility depends on a borrowing base, and the revolver's springing first lien net leverage covenant of 7.10x was not in effect at June 30, 2026, so headroom cannot be measured. The next significant maturities are USD 1,324.6 million in 2028 (the 7.750% notes and the term loan) and USD 906.3 million in 2029, which together are about 43.3% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending merger dominates the capital structure outlook. The take-private merger at USD 2.43 per share was approved by stockholders on May 12, 2026 and was expected to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026, but its first outside date of November 9, 2026 falls four days after the cutoff and the supplied sources do not say whether it closed. Debt amendments make the merger not a change of control, but they become operative only on closing, and conditional redemption notices cover the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes. The funding source and price of those redemptions and the buyer's financing are not supplied. Equity consideration on basic shares is about USD 1,237.1 million, about 24.0% of debt principal, so the offer implies a thin equity layer beneath the debt (Analyst Interpretation; no valuation or recovery view is stated).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is short-cycle revenue against fixed rent. Roadside advertising is mostly sold in four-week periods while site leases and municipal and airport concessions run for years, so a demand dip reaches margin before contracts roll. Airports Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.3% in H1 2026 against 41.0% for America because airport site lease expense was 59.2% of revenue, and airport minimum guarantees rise with prior-period performance. Revenue grew 8.7% in the second quarter of 2026 and Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.6%, partly on event-driven demand from the FIFA World Cup (Documentary Fact; the event effect is Analyst Interpretation as to repeatability).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Earnings momentum: trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 544.3 million is above the FY2025 level of USD 504.8 million, and H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA grew about 19.0% over H1 2025 (Documentary Fact). Permit-protected, diversified inventory: more than 64,500 displays and operations in 81 U.S. markets at December 31, 2025, and no single advertiser is a material portion of revenue (Documentary Fact; the leading-position claims are Management Language and are not adopted). Liquidity and runway: USD 192.1 million of cash, USD 205.5 million of undrawn facilities maturing in June 2030, and no significant maturities before 2028 (Documentary Fact). Simplified, domestic business: substantially all international operations were sold, with the Spain sale completed on August 4, 2026, which simplifies the perimeter (Documentary Fact). No distributions: no dividends are intended and none are permitted while the merger agreement stands (Documentary Fact). Positive free cash flow: USD 84.3 million on the trailing basis against USD 32.0 million in FY2025 (Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the measure).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. High leverage with flat debt: 9.46x total debt and 9.11x net, with principal essentially unchanged, so deleveraging relies on earnings and asset sale proceeds (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). Thin cover: cash interest cover of 1.40x and about 1.20x after capital expenditure leave limited room for an advertising downturn, and the stockholders' deficit is USD 3,457.1 million (Documentary Fact). Fixed airport rent: airport site lease expense at 59.2% of revenue makes the fastest-growing segment the lowest-margin one, and USD 1,361.9 million of operating lease liabilities sit outside the debt figure (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Refinancing concentration: about 43.3% of principal falls due in 2028 and 2029, and the unsecured notes rank behind USD 3,340.0 million of secured debt (Documentary Fact). Metro and sector concentration: America is about three quarters of revenue, Los Angeles is a leading market, and 2026 growth drew on technology advertisers in the San Francisco area (Documentary Fact). Unresolved ownership and merger outcome: control, merger financing, the post-closing capital plan and the consent terms are not supplied, and willingness of the prospective owner cannot be inferred from its identity (Insufficient Information). Information limits: covenant headroom, guarantor financials and executed documents are not supplied (Insufficient Information).
